first.rationale: The two degrading metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point directly at the funnel stage that memory_86 and memory_31 address, so onboarding/signup simplification is the intervention whose mechanism matches the observed problem rather than the loudest external pressure. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records that it wins acquisition and revenue up front but materially damages 30-day retention, and it explicitly warns against generalizing it — that is a direct conflict with the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Referral incentives (memory_57) are clean but target established customers, not the leaking top of funnel; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment entirely and does not touch the SMB self-serve decline. I am spending both verification pulls on the memories that actually underwrite my chosen action rather than on the ones I am rejecting, because rejecting promo pricing is safe under either reading of memory_73 while acting on memory_86/memory_31 is not. The specific thing I want from the archive is whether the recorded lifts were measured on downstream qualified revenue and retention or only on upstream funnel metrics. memory_31 claims a 'durable' first-week activation lift and memory_86 claims improved completion and time-to-value — but completion rate is exactly the kind of proxy that can be inflated by removing friction that was doing useful qualifying work. Cutting required fields can raise activation counts while admitting lower-intent accounts, which is structurally the same failure mode memory_73 documents: a real upstream win that inverts downstream. I also want to check whether memory_86 and memory_31 are genuinely independent evidence or two consolidations of overlapping experiments, since treating one result as two would overstate my confidence. Contingency: if the source records show revenue/retention were tracked and held, I proceed at standard experiment scale with qualified-revenue and 30-day retention as gating metrics, not activation. If they show only funnel-proxy measurement, or if the two memories collapse into one underlying test, I downscale to a small guarded test with a holdout and an explicit lead-quality check before any broader rollout. Activation_messaging (memory_91) is the fallback if simplification looks proxy-inflated, since it adds a nudge without removing qualifying friction.

final.rationale:
Verification paid off, and it split the two memories apart rather than confirming them together. exp_31 (signup simplification, SMB) is genuinely clean on the metric that matters: qualified revenue +4% with 30-day retention essentially flat at -1%. That is a downstream-validated result, not a proxy win, and it is the one piece of evidence here that directly underwrites the objective. exp_86 is the opposite: the consolidated memory said 'improved completion and time-to-value' and silently dropped 60-day churn +9% concentrated in complex-workspace accounts, plus an explicit do-not-roll-out instruction. This is exactly the proxy-inflation failure mode I flagged — shortening the flow removes setup steps that complex workspaces actually need, so the completion lift was partly friction that was doing real work. The two memories were also not independent confirmation of one idea; they are different interventions with opposite risk profiles.

Decision: run signup simplification (reduced required fields at signup) scoped to SMB self-serve accounts only, at standard experiment scale, with complex-workspace accounts explicitly excluded and the exp_86-style shortening of substantive setup steps NOT included. This is the intervention with verified downstream support, and it targets the actual observed decline in the self-serve funnel.

I reject promotional_pricing despite the competitor pressure being the loudest signal in the room: memory_73 records acquisition and revenue lift paired with material 30-day retention damage and an explicit warning against generalizing it. Meeting a price attack with a retention-destroying instrument trades long-term qualified revenue for a quarter of vanity acquisition. referral_incentive (memory_57) is clean but addresses established customers, not the leaking top of funnel. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment and does not touch the SMB decline driving the numbers.

Residual uncertainty I am not papering over: exp_31 was explicitly not replicated outside SMB, so I hold it to SMB and make no claim about other segments. The -1% retention is small but directionally negative, and the +4% qualified revenue came from a single run — I will gate on qualified revenue and 30/60-day retention with a holdout, not on signup or activation counts, since exp_86 just demonstrated how badly funnel proxies can mislead here. If 60-day retention degrades or the qualified-revenue lift does not reproduce, I stop rather than scale. Activation_messaging (memory_91) remains the fallback for a later slot; it adds a nudge without removing qualifying friction, but it is still only proxy-validated on week-one engagement and would need its own downstream check. I am also flagging that memory_86 as consolidated is actively misleading and should be corrected in durable memory to carry the complex-workspace churn caveat.
